summary: CRLF characters injected into Azure AD role claim cause ingress header truncation and missing RBAC bindings in private VPC
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403s for their service accounts and scheduled workers in a private VPC. Failures correlate with specific users and automated jobs that have recently onboarded via Azure AD synchronization. Impact: Several backend scheduled workers and a subset of tenant admins were unable to access admin console and API, causing delayed batch processing and customer-visible errors. Environment: Private deployment (NimbusFintech) in us-east; ingress is an edge-proxy with header forwarding to internal auth-assertion-parser. Observed behavior: authz decision shows no role bindings attached even though Azure AD shows roles present on the user. Initial hypothesis: assertion or header truncation caused RBAC service to receive incomplete role list. This ticket captures triage, investigation, and remediation timeline.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure Azure AD SAML integration and enable group-to-role mapping in the Nimbus tenant (private deployment).
2) Create a test user with a role claim value that contains a newline/carriage-return sequence (copy pasted or generated by certain AD provisioning flows).
3) Trigger login or service token exchange via the ingress edge-proxy (simulate scheduled worker flow).

4) Observe logs at ingress and auth-assertion-parser: ingress receives Assertion, but header forwarded to backend truncates after first line; RBAC service shows empty role array and denies admin-scoped endpoints.
5) Reproduce intermittently — only some sync paths create the CRLF in claim value.

investigation_notes: 03/13 10:00 - Customer supplied raw SAML assertion XML; claim element <Attribute Name="roles"> contains value with '\r\n' in several entries produced by AD Connect job.

03/13 11:20 - Edge-proxy codepath uses naive header serialization (folds values, does NOT RFC-compress or sanitize control chars), which results in an HTTP header with embedded CRLF sequence; many downstream HTTP libraries treat that as header boundary and drop remainder.

03/13 12:05 - Confirmed truncation occurs in edge-router -> auth-assertion-parser hop; parser receives only substring before CRLF, hence RBAC mapping fails (no fallback to full assertion parsing in current pipeline).
03/13 13:30 - Reproduced locally by injecting CRLF into role attribute; same behavior. Unit test added to repro locally for engineering.

Hypothesis: Upstream Azure AD provisioning pipeline occasionally introduces CRLFs when concatenating group display names; edge-proxy should sanitize before header emission or forward assertion via POST body rather than inline header.
comments: 2026-03-13T14:02 - Lena Ortiz (Support): Notified customer that we have a reproducible case and escalated to Infra team. Asked for number of affected service accounts and temporary mitigation options.

2026-03-13T14:20 - Marcus Chen (Infra): Confirmed edge-proxy header serialization is the weak point. Suggested temporary rule to reject control characters and log instances with full assertion to secure S3 bucket for debug. Marked for immediate hotfix.

2026-03-13T15:10 - Nimbus support contact (Rajiv Kumar): Provided AD Connect export sample and consent to scrub and share assertion snapshots. Requested ETA for workaround because nightly jobs are failing.

2026-03-13T16:05 - Marcus Chen (Infra): Deployed ingress config to sanitize control characters (strip CRLF) at proxy-level as a staged mitigation in prod-us-east. Informed customer to retest scheduled jobs.
2026-03-13T16:22 - Nimbus (Rajiv Kumar): Confirmed scheduled worker run succeeded after mitigation; some historical events still failed — requested root cause and permanent patch timeline.
resolution: Mitigation applied: ingress edge-proxy updated with control-character sanitization rule (strip CR and LF from header values) rolled to 50% canary then all nodes in prod-us-east. Customer confirmed immediate improvement for failing scheduled jobs.

Permanent fix: Engineering to ship parser hardening in edge-proxy: validate and escape or move long structured claims to POST body instead of headers; add defense-in-depth in auth-assertion-parser to parse full SAML assertion when header parsing yields truncated/malformed results.
Rollback/rollout notes: Canary started 2026-03-13T16:05; full rollout complete 2026-03-13T17:00. No service regression observed in 60m canary window.
Customer communication: Advised Nimbus to sanitize group names in AD Connect as a hygiene step; provided recommended transformation regex and a Confluence doc link.
